raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL (`python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/kernel_templates/*`, `kernel_registry.py`)
- Benchmarks or performance

## Summary

Every SM120 Frost template now creates its A and B data TMA descriptors with `l2_promotion=l2_128b` (the 512-byte scale-factor atoms are left alone), and `Sm120KernelTemplate.multi_gemm_smem_bytes` sizes the packed e2m1 side of a mixed MXFP4 x MXFP8 pair at its real 64-byte SMEM row, as `multi_gemm_ab_stages` and the kernel's ring layout already did. One commit, 9769e15b.

## Why

The templates called `cutlass.experimental.cuda.tensor_map.create_tensor_map_tiled` without an `l2_promotion`, so the descriptors carried the DSL default (none) instead of CUTLASS's 128-byte promotion. A box whose K row is 64 bytes then issues one DRAM request per row. That is exactly the packed e2m1 side of a mixed MXFP4 x MXFP8 pair (a 128-element fp8 K tile holds 128 e2m1 values in 64 B) and any 64-byte K tile.

Measured on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 188 SMs), CUDA 13.4, cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, driver 615.71.09, through FlashInfer's unified MoE benchmark (CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, per-backend autotune):

- The MXFP8 x MXFP4 MoE kernels were TMA bound at 0.85 TB/s while the NVFP4 and MXFP8 kernels of the same tile (128-byte rows) streamed at 1.19 TB/s. Removing the mainloop's MMAs, fragment loads and scale loads left the time unchanged, as did 2 to 4 ring stages and a padded one-byte-per-value e2m1 form (see the sibling PR for that experiment). A standalone TMA streaming test of the same boxes reproduces 0.85 vs 1.19 TB/s with promotion none vs `l2_128b`, and shows no difference for 128-byte rows.
- Kernel level, 12-expert 7168x3072 MoE at 16 tokens: FC1 342.8 -> 253.4 us, FC2 129.4 -> 98.1 us; the CuTe-DSL SM12x mixed-input kernels take 251.4 / 97.8 us. Whole MoE call kernel time 473 -> 365 us (SM12x 353 us).
- 40-case matrix (8 shapes x T = 1/16/128/1024/4096, same session A/B): Frost MXFP8 x MXFP4 time becomes 0.883x of before (geomean; T=1 0.86x, T=16 0.81x, T=128 0.84x, T=1024 0.91x, T=4096 0.99x, the last being compute bound). Against the fastest other FlashInfer backend (CUTLASS / cuTile / SM12x) Frost moves from 0.863x to 0.966x; with FlashInfer's stage budgeting following the corrected footprint it reaches 0.997x of SM12x (17 of 35 cases not slower).
- BF16 tiles with a 64-byte K tile load the same way and should gain similarly (not measured separately).

FlashInfer's frozen SM120 MXFP8 x MXFP4 catalog (`flashinfer/fused_moe/backends/cudnn_frost/artifacts/mxfp8_mxfp4`) was re-exported from this commit: all 754 kernel ids are unchanged, only the rendered sources change (the `l2_promotion` lines).

Related PRs from the same investigation: #1881 (scheduler-counter knob, stacked on this PR) and #1882 (the padded e2m1 experiment this fix supersedes).

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API change. Supported GPU / cuDNN / CUDA / Python versions unchanged.
- Rendered SM120 kernel sources change (the descriptor hint and the footprint check), so consumers that pin exported sources must re-export to pick up the change; the gated mixed FC1 tiles gain one to two ring stages from the corrected footprint.
- Performance: see above; the SM100 templates are untouched.

## Testing

Run on 2026-10-26 on the RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) above, from this checkout with the frost test conftest overlaying `python/cudnn/gemm/frost` ahead of the installed wheel (the conftest change in this PR):

```
cd cudnn-frontend && git checkout sm120-moe-tma-l2-promotion
CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<sm120 gpu> python -m pytest \
  test/python/gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist \
  -k "mixed_mxfp8_mxfp4_sm120 or smem_footprint or render_smoke"
```

- New tests: `test_e2e_mixed_mxfp8_mxfp4_sm120` (both orientations and operand orders, whole K tiles and a K tail, against a dequantized reference; pins the rendered descriptors), `test_dual_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swiglu_mixed_sm120` (gated two-weight kernel), `test_sm120_mixed_pair_smem_footprint_budgets_packed_rows`, and the render smoke test pins the hint. Render smoke / footprint tests: 14 passed.
- The SM120 MoE test selection across `test/python/gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_*matmul_fwd*.py`: 630 passed on the SM120 GPU.
- FlashInfer side, with the re-exported catalog: `tests/moe/test_cudnn_frost_{catalog,manifest,kernels}.py` (mxfp8_mxfp4 / sm120 / shortlist subset) + `test_unified_moe_frost.py`: 258 passed / 118 skipped / 0 failed.
- Not re-run at PR creation time: both SM120 GPUs on the host are occupied by a benchmark run. 16 frost tests in `test_tile_select_analytic.py` / `test_block_scale_matmul.py` / `test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py` fail on an SM120-only host on unpatched develop as well (they assume an SM100 GPU); they are not regressions of this PR.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: clang-format skipped (no C++), black / black-jupyter / SPDX license header passed.

Walkthrough
The change adjusts SMEM sizing for mixed-width FP4 operands, sets 128-byte L2 promotion on SM120 A/B TMA descriptors, and adds tests for mixed-width grouped matmul and SwiGLU cases. **Changes: SM120 GEMM updates** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Mixed-width SMEM sizing**
`python/cudnn/gemm/frost/kernel_registry.py`|Mixed-width block-scale operands now use half the K-byte span to size the FP4 side’s tile.| |**TMA L2 promotion**
